podcast.body: "Yellow Ledbetter" first appeared on a European CD single for "Jeremy" in 1992, meaning North American fans had to hunt for high-priced imports. A live version appeared on a Japanese CD single for "Daughter." Eddie Vedder mumbles through much of it, so internet lyric transcriptions are rough approximations; Eddie frequently improvises the words live and rarely follows the official lyrics. Some fans consider it the greatest Pearl Jam song ever recorded and it might have been a worldwide hit had it been released as a single. The song is actually named after a real person: Tim Ledbetter, an old friend of Eddie Vedder from Chicago — an inside joke. "There really is someone named Yellow Lead Better. Except that his first name is Tim."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: "Yellow Ledbetter" was originally released as a bonus track on an imported version of the "Jeremy" CD single. This exemplifies a type of music discovery that is fading, where unique tracks were found on specific international or extended single releases. "There's no more finding a song like Yellow Lead Better from Pearl Jam, which was originally a bonus track on an imported version of the Jeremy CD single."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
